stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Tag, an agentic AI teammate that lives inside Slack

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Claude Tag on June 23, 2026, a product that embeds Claude inside Slack as a persistent, shared teammate that anyone on a team can delegate work to by typing @Claude.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Tag is a new way for teams to work with Claude. We're starting on Slack, which Claude can join as a team member. Grant Claude access to selected channels, and connect it to whichever tools, data—and even codebases—you choose.

key_facts.fact: Claude Tag is available in beta for Claude Enterprise and Team customers and replaces the existing 'Claude in Slack' app, which will be retired (administrators have 30 days to opt in to migration).
key_facts.excerpt: It's available today in beta for Claude Enterprise and Team customers... Claude Tag replaces the existing Claude in Slack app. To migrate, administrators can opt in within 30 days.

key_facts.fact: When assigned a task, Claude Tag breaks it into stages, executes them using whichever connected tools it has access to, retains context and memory across channels, and can act proactively in an 'ambient' mode.
key_facts.excerpt: When assigned a task, Claude Tag breaks it into stages and works through them using whichever tools it has access to... the more notable feature is an ambient mode that proactively jumps into conversations to keep teams updated.

key_facts.fact: The product runs on Claude Opus 4.8, the model Anthropic released less than a month earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: The product runs on Claude Opus 4.8, the model Anthropic released less than a month ago.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is offering launch credits to drive adoption: $25,000 worth of credits for Enterprise customers and $2,500 for Team customers, applicable only to Tag usage in Slack; the old Claude-in-Slack connector leaves service on August 3.
key_facts.excerpt: Enterprise customers who add Tag to Slack will get $25,000 worth of credits, while Teams customers will get $2,500... the existing connector will leave service on August 3.

stories.headline: Nvidia launches BioNeMo Agent Toolkit to bring agentic AI to drug discovery

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced the BioNeMo Agent Toolkit on June 23, 2026, providing domain-specific, agent-callable tools and skills for protein structure prediction, molecular docking, generative chemistry, genomic analysis, protein design and biomarker discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA today announced NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit, which provides domain-specific tools and skills for the agentic life sciences era... agent-callable skills for tasks including protein structure prediction, molecular docking, generative chemistry, genomic analysis, protein design and biomarker discovery.

key_facts.fact: More than 50 leading companies are already using the toolkit; adopters and integrators include Dassault Systèmes, Databricks, Lilly, Schrödinger, Snowflake and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design, with Anthropic and OpenAI integrating it.
key_facts.excerpt: Industry and research leaders including Dassault Systèmes, Databricks, Lilly, Schrödinger, Snowflake, the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design and dozens others are adopting, and Anthropic and OpenAI are integrating, NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's collaboration with the UW Institute for Protein Design accelerated runtimes for biodesign models like RosettaFold3 to 2x faster than the prior generation, and the toolkit compresses virtual screening timelines from days to minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: The IPD collaboration has accelerated runtimes for state-of-the-art biodesign models like RosettaFold3, resulting in 2x faster performance than the prior-generation model... compressing screening timelines from days to minutes.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia reports that agents using BioNeMo Skills complete biomolecular tasks with a 2x improvement in token efficiency compared with agents without the tools.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA reports significant efficiency gains: agents using BioNeMo Skills complete biomolecular tasks with a 2x improvement in token efficiency (the computational cost of running models) compared to agents without these tools.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia healthcare GM Kimberly Powell framed the launch as the start of an 'agentic life sciences era,' arguing agentic AI is poised to do for biotech what it did for software.
key_facts.excerpt: Kimberly Powell, vice president and general manager of healthcare and life sciences at Nvidia Corp., made the case that agentic AI is about to do for biotech what it just did for software.

stories.headline: Mistral releases OCR 4 with bounding boxes and confidence scores across 170 languages

key_facts.fact: Mistral released OCR 4 on June 23, 2026, a document-intelligence model that returns bounding boxes, typed-block classification (titles, tables, equations, signatures) and inline confidence scores alongside extracted text, supporting 170 languages across 10 language groups.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're releasing Mistral OCR 4, featuring bounding boxes, block classification, and inline confidence scores alongside extracted text. The model supports 170 languages across 10 language groups, runs in a single container for fully self-hosted deployments.

key_facts.fact: In a blind human evaluation across 600+ real-world documents in 12+ languages, independent annotators preferred OCR 4 over every leading OCR and document-AI system tested, with win rates averaging 72%.
key_facts.excerpt: Independent annotators prefer OCR 4 over every leading OCR and document-AI system tested, with win rates averaging 72%, alongside the top overall score on OlmOCRBench (85.20).

key_facts.fact: OCR 4 achieves the top overall score on the public OlmOCRBench (85.20) and scores 93.07 on OmniDocBench, though Mistral cautions the aggregate automated scores are directional given known benchmark scoring limitations.
key_facts.excerpt: OCR 4 achieves the top overall score amongst the models we tested on the public OlmOCRBench (85.20)... On OmniDocBench, OCR 4 achieves a score of 93.07. We report this figure with a caveat.

key_facts.fact: OCR 4 is priced at $4 per 1,000 pages via API (dropping to $2 with a 50% Batch-API discount) and is available through Mistral Studio, Amazon SageMaker and Microsoft Foundry, with a single-container self-hosting option.
key_facts.excerpt: Mistral OCR 4 through the API is priced at $4 per 1,000 pages, with a 50% Batch-API discount, reducing the cost to $2 per 1,000 pages... available via API through Mistral Studio, Amazon SageMaker, Microsoft Foundry.

stories.headline: Krea releases open weights for its Krea 2 image model under a custom license

key_facts.fact: On June 23, 2026, AI creative-tools startup Krea released the open weights of its Krea 2 image model as two checkpoints, 'Krea 2 Raw' (an undistilled base for fine-tuning) and 'Krea 2 Turbo' (a fast distilled version), available for download on Hugging Face.
key_facts.excerpt: Krea is hoping to change that trend by opening up the weights to its new frontier AI image model Krea 2 as two versions, 'Krea 2 Raw' and 'Krea 2 Turbo'... Both models are available for public download on Hugging Face.

key_facts.fact: Krea 2 is built on a Diffusion Transformer scaled to 12 billion parameters trained from scratch; the Turbo variant renders native 2K-resolution images in roughly 2 seconds using an 8-step inference pipeline, among the fastest open or proprietary image models.
key_facts.excerpt: At the technical core of the release sits an architectural framework built entirely from scratch: a Diffusion Transformer scaled to 12 billion parameters... Krea 2 Turbo slashes the required generation cycle down to just 8 inference steps... in approximately 2 seconds.

key_facts.fact: The Krea 2 Community License lets individuals and small companies use the weights royalty-free but requires firms with more than 50 seats to pay for an enterprise license, and mandates all deployers implement content classifiers to block illegal, NCII, CSAM or defamatory outputs.
key_facts.excerpt: a custom license that requires firms with more than 50 seats to pay for Enterprise usage, and mandates all users of any size to implement technical safeguards to prevent the generation of illegal materials, non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), child sexual abuse material (CSAM), or defamatory assets.

key_facts.fact: Krea, founded in 2022 in San Francisco, has raised $83 million in disclosed venture funding (backers include Andreessen Horowitz and Bain Capital Ventures) and surpassed 30 million users across 191 countries as of June 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: an aggregate $83 million in disclosed venture capital funding from major VCs including Andreessen Horowitz and Bain Capital Ventures... The company's user base surpassed 30 million individuals across 191 countries as of June 2026.

sources.title: Enterprise-grade AI image generation in 2 seconds is here: Krea 2 Raw and Turbo available as open weights under custom license

stories.headline: Engram exits stealth with $98M to build a learned memory layer for AI

key_facts.fact: Engram emerged from stealth on June 23, 2026 with $98 million in funding from General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Factory, Modern, Amplify Partners and Neo, plus angels including Wiz CEO Assaf Rappaport, OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy and AI/robotics researcher Pieter Abbeel.
key_facts.excerpt: Engram, the company building the learned memory layer for AI, emerged from stealth with $98M in funding from General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Factory, Modern, Amplify Partners, Neo and notable angels and advisors including Assaf Rappaport, co-founder and CEO of Wiz, Andrej Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI, and Pieter Abbeel.

key_facts.fact: The round values Engram at $600 million; the company has just 13 employees and was founded in October 2025 out of Stanford University's AI lab, led by CEO Dr. Dan Biderman.
key_facts.excerpt: The American startup Engram... has completed a $98 million funding round at a $600 million valuation... 'We founded the company last October directly out of Stanford University's AI lab,' Biderman, who serves as the company's CEO, told.

key_facts.fact: Engram builds models that study an organization's data in advance to form a compact, continuously improving memory, which it says matches or outperforms frontier models while using just 1-10% of the tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: Engram compresses that knowledge into reusable model memory that matches or outperforms frontier models while using 1-10% of the tokens. The AI gets smarter the more you use it, and you own the memories.

key_facts.fact: Engram has a partnership with Microsoft to test its models within Microsoft 365, including a commitment to GPU capacity across Dapple and Azure, aimed at making enterprise AI more efficient and context-aware.
key_facts.excerpt: Engram enters the market with meaningful early commercial traction, anchored by a partnership with Microsoft. The two companies are working together to test Engram's models within Microsoft 365... The partnership also includes a commitment to GPU capacity across Dapple and Azure.

sources.title: Engram Launches with $98M to Build AI That Actually Knows Your Organization

stories.headline: Probook raises $40M from a16z and Sequoia to build an AI OS for home services

key_facts.fact: Probook announced on June 23, 2026 that it raised $40 million, comprising a $34 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz and a previously completed $6 million seed round led by Sequoia Capital, which also joined the Series A.
key_facts.excerpt: a16z is leading Probook's $34 million Series A, bringing the company's total funding to $40 million after a seed round led by Sequoia.

key_facts.fact: Probook is building an AI operating system for home-service businesses (plumbing, HVAC, electrical, maintenance), automating dispatch, scheduling, customer communication and data verification, starting with the hard problem of routing the right technician.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup is building an AI operating system for home service businesses, automating dispatch, scheduling, and customer communications... The company is building software that automates dispatch, customer communication, data verification, and scheduling.

key_facts.fact: Probook runs across hundreds of locations nationwide; Summers Plumbing, Heating & Cooling (14 locations, 260 technicians) booked 2,542 jobs in its first month on the platform with zero human intervention, and Del-Air more than doubled productivity from 10 to 22 techs per dispatcher.
key_facts.excerpt: Summers Plumbing, Heating & Cooling, with 14 locations and 260 technicians on the platform, booked 2,542 jobs in its first month on Probook with zero human intervention. Del-Air more than doubled productivity from 10 to 22 techs per dispatcher.

stories.headline: Menlo Ventures raises $3B, its largest-ever fund, to go all-in on AI

key_facts.fact: Menlo Ventures announced on June 23, 2026 that it raised $3 billion in new capital, the largest raise in the firm's 50-year history, dedicated to backing AI startups across enterprise, healthcare and consumer markets.
key_facts.excerpt: Menlo Ventures announced $3 billion in funds on Tuesday, the largest raise in its 50-year history, driven in large part by its AI portfolio, especially Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: The capital is split across two funds: Menlo Ventures XVII for seed and Series A startups, and Menlo Inflection IV, a growth fund for Series B and later companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The firm's new capital is across two funds: Menlo Ventures XVII, earmarked for seed and Series A startups, and Menlo Inflection IV, a growth fund for Series B and later startups.

key_facts.fact: Menlo's stake in Anthropic is now worth about $14 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, after the firm made a 'bet-the-firm' $750 million investment leading Anthropic's 2024 Series D and invested in every round since.
key_facts.excerpt: Its stake in the model maker is now worth about $14 billion, sources told Bloomberg... they made a bet-the-firm $750 million investment in Anthropic in 2024, preemptively leading the model maker's Series D.

key_facts.fact: Menlo first invested in Anthropic in 2023 when it was pre-product and pre-revenue, and in July 2024 launched the $100 million Menlo Anthology Fund in partnership with Anthropic, which has since backed more than 60 companies with several exits.
key_facts.excerpt: We made our first investment in Anthropic in 2023, when the company was pre-product, pre-revenue... In July 2024, we launched the Menlo Anthology Fund in partnership with them... The fund has now backed more than 60 companies.
